node2.text:
One card, three steps: sync → bring history over → switch.

• Step 3 is always visible, disabled with its reason, instead of the Switch button vanishing.
• The recommended path and the date path are two choices up front, not a hidden “Advanced” toggle.
• Every running state names its phase and shows progress; “Preparing” replaces the bare “Processing the current batch…”.
• The node log moves behind a button; Rescan and Block retention become rows under Advanced node tools, disabled with a reason while recovery runs.

Needs an engine change: today “Import” fetches and scans EVERY block from the Vault's oldest coin to the tip, 32 at a time, from Bitcoin peers. The “fetches only the blocks that hold payments Connect found” copy assumes a targeted fetch of just those blocks.

Block numbers and dates are sample values.

wiz2.text:
Proposal (2026-11-04)

1. Launcher button reads “Import or restore Bitcoin wallet” and always opens on Overview.
2. Network lives in the modal head as the same menu in both wizards (no separate Network step in Create). Preselected from the Launcher's Network filter.
3. One frame for Create, Import, Connect and App preferences: a sheet over the dimmed Launcher, the normal top bar above it, Close top right. No “Back to Cube list”; Back lives in the sheet footer.
4. Import or restore works on every network. Only the wallet-import row is limited to Bitcoin and Bitcoin Blake2b, with the reason inline and a one-click switch. On other networks its nav item and Start are disabled; the import screen is never shown there.
5. Restores and imports set a PIN only: a passkey can't hold a secret brought in from outside. Create keeps Passkey or PIN.

tfa_n1.text:
For review (updated 2026-11-16). Nothing is built in the app yet.

Where it lives
• Connect account › Devices & security gets an "Authenticator app" group at the top, above Verified Devices. Once on, a second row shows "Backup codes · N of 10 left" with "Make new codes…".
• Account › Sign-in method names it and links there.
• Everything opens inline under the rows, the same way Sign out and Remove device do. No modal.

Turning it on
• Scan the QR (or copy the setup key), then type one code. Nothing changes until that code checks out.
• Next, the 10 backup codes are shown once, with Copy all, Save as text file and "I've saved them".

Backup codes
• Each works once in place of an authenticator code: to finish signing in, or to turn the app off.
• At 3 or fewer left, the row turns amber. "Make new codes" needs a code from the app and invalidates the old set.

Turning it off
• With a current code from the app, or "Use a backup code instead". The account gets an email.
• The emailed turn-off link was dropped here: it opens a website page that needs a login the site no longer has.

Sign-in
• After the email code, accounts with an authenticator get a third step. "Use a backup code instead" switches the field.
• Signing in with a backup code shows how many are left; at 3 or fewer it says to make a new set now.
• "No app and no backup codes?" explains the way back in.
• States: wrong code, wrong backup code, too many tries (5 per 5 minutes), timed out, lost both.

API: coincubetech/coincube-api#476 (draft). Desktop still ignores requires_2fa today; this step fixes that.

QR, setup key, codes, dates and support contact are samples or placeholders.

mvTitle.text: Overview · three changes that bring Desktop closer to Mobile V3

mvNote.text: Three changes only. 1 Buttons: Receive is a neutral outline with a down arrow, Send is filled with an up arrow, and Receive comes first, as on Mobile (40 px tall, 10 px corners). 2 Artwork: none on Overview. 3 Fill, not outlines: cards, the backup strip and menus have no border. Regions of the window (top bar, sidebar, page title) keep a dividing line in a quieter colour, ink at 10%, as Mobile uses; hairlines also stay between rows. Also changed: the wordmark is one colour with Mobile's letter spacing, and menu rows use a medium weight. Left alone on purpose: the status chips in the top bar, the table, type sizes and all wording. Each board keeps the Overview levers (page, theme, review state), so the same changes can be seen on the Spark and Vault pages.

mvCube.text: Second pass (Robert, 2026-11-26). The Cube sits above the Cube selector and fills most of the sidebar's width. Four faces, turning as Mobile's Cube does: Overview, Wallets, Activity, Settings, with the face you are on lit at the front left and the next one showing at the right. Click a sidebar item, or a face on the Cube. Spark and Vault share the Wallets face; Backup & protection shows the Settings face; Marketplace is not on a face yet. Levers: page; unlock (once, loop, off); payment arrived (the Activity face turns green); backup confirmed (the Settings gear is amber until it is); test network (dashed edges and a tag). Unlock: the Cube pulses in the middle of the window, then shrinks and travels to its place while the page fades in. The Launcher is not changed. The sheet below shows the four poses, the states and the unlock as still frames. The first pass, a small Cube at the top right of the sidebar, is in this canvas's version history (version 315 and earlier).

mvNoticesTitle.text: Notices and status · today in the app, and proposed

mvNotices.text: Left: what the app shows today, on a test-network Cube with balances hidden, the backup not confirmed, one warning and one error. Seen in the running app on 2026-11-25: the blue bar, the orange hide toggle, the boxed backup strip. Drawn from the app's code, not seen live: the orange warning block and the outlined error card. Right: one treatment for all of them, taken from the toasts (Tenshu Toasts, Nov 2026). Each notice is a filled row with its tone in a small icon tile, a title, one line and at most one action. The test network becomes a tag beside the wordmark, on every page. Hide balances turns neutral when on, and the eyes beside each section step back while everything is hidden. The backup strip becomes one line. Not changed: the single Connect control with its status light is already how the app works; the older boards still show two chips. The notice wording is sample text. Levers: All clear shows the same screen with nothing to report; Hide balances and theme work as before.

mvTilesTitle.text: Receive and Send · the two dropdown tiles, today and proposed

mvTiles.text: Receive and Send share one pattern: two dropdown tiles joined by an arrow. Today boards redraw the running app (signed local build, 2026-11-25). Proposed keeps both tiles and changes how they are drawn. 1 No card around the form: the tiles sit on the page as a fill with no outline, so there is one level where the app has three. 2 The tile's type drops a step and the coin icon is smaller. 3 The lists lead with what differs. Today four rows read Bitcoin and differ only by a small orange tag; proposed groups them under Bitcoin and names the method. Stablecoins take one row each, with the networks as chips, so the Receive list fits without scrolling (seven rows where the app has twelve). 4 The selected row is a neutral fill with a tick, not brown and orange. 5 Fields keep their outlines, as controls do; the dividers between them are gone, and the button is the 40 px pill. Wording is the app's, rearranged; the stablecoin chips are a layout change to check. Levers: Open (closed, first, second) shows either list; the tiles also open on click. Both tiles are pickers on both pages: on Receive, You receive is Bitcoin or US Dollar (USDB) in Spark; on Send, You send is Bitcoin or US Dollar (USDB) in Spark. Each has its own board with that list open.

mvTypeTitle.text: Type scale · Desktop on Mobile V3's steps

mvType.text: Desktop and Mobile already share the typeface and weights. The sizes differ. Proposed: the large sizes take Mobile V3's steps (main amount 40 to 46, page title 22 to 26, section title 18 to 20), and the odd sizes go (12.5, 34), which leaves 8 sizes on Overview where there are 12. Running text stays as it is, one step under Mobile (rows 14 where Mobile has 16, secondary lines 13 where Mobile has 14), because a Desktop window holds more per screen. To see every step at Mobile's size, set the text lever on the right-hand board to as Mobile: rows grow to 16 and some lines start to wrap. Mobile sizes are read from the Mobile V3 prototype; Desktop sizes from the Overview study board. The right-hand board keeps the page lever, so the same sizes can be checked on the Spark, Vault and Backup pages.

retNote.text: These boards draw screens the app no longer has (checked against COINCUBE Desktop master 088c9f9). The Liquid wallet is gone; the only Liquid the app still shows is "USDt on Liquid" as a SideShift receive option. "Claim" in the app means making a Bitcoin Blake2b copy Cube, now drawn on "Bitcoin Blake2b copy". Kept here for reference, not linked from the prototype. The two "state collection" boards (P-GapsDetails, P-GapsWallets) were retired on 2026-11-26 after every state moved onto its owner board as a lever.

protoTitle.text: COINCUBE Desktop V3 · clickable prototype (source of truth)

protoNote.text: Checked against the running app, master 088c9f9, on 2026-11-26 (signed local build on scratch data, plus a code inventory for signed-in, Vault, Marketplace and Duress screens). Boards show what the app does today, plus the V3 decisions that deliberately differ: no worldview artwork (Overview, opening, App preferences); Receive before Send; fills instead of outlines; one Connect control in the top bar; the test network as a tag beside the wordmark; notices in the toast anatomy; the decided Receive/Send tiles; display sizes on Mobile's steps with running text one step under. The Cube in the sidebar is not part of V3 (see the study page). Liquid is gone; its boards, and the two former gap boards, are on "Retired". Most boards have levers for the app's other states (signed out, no Vault, errors, gated features).

mvFolded.text: 2026-11-26: the decided studies (notices and status, Receive/Send tiles, type scale) are folded into the clickable prototype, which is the source of truth for V3. The Cube in the sidebar is left out for now and recorded in the Desktop plan as a possible future direction.
